proofs.proof_tex:
By the observation and additive-effect assumptions,
\[
Y_1=Y^{\mathrm{post}}(1)=\Lambda G+E_1+\beta\mathbf 1_{T_1}^{\top}.
\]
Multiplication by \(T_1^{-1}\mathbf 1_{T_1}\), together with the definition of \(a\), gives
\[
z=\Lambda a+\beta+T_1^{-1}E_1\mathbf 1_{T_1}=m+\beta+\eta,
\;
\eta=T_1^{-1}E_1\mathbf 1_{T_1}.
\]
The entries of \(E_1\) are mutually independent \(\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\) variables by the Gaussian-error assumption.  Hence linearity of Gaussian laws yields
\[
\eta\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2 I_N/T_1).
\]
The same assumption makes \(E_1\) independent of \(E_0\).  Since \(Y_0=\Lambda F+E_0\) and the remaining quantities in this expression are deterministic parameters, \(\eta\) is independent of \(Y_0\).  None of these steps uses centered post-factor variation: if \(G=a\mathbf 1_{T_1}^{\top}\), the same calculation applies verbatim.  Finally, the additive potential-outcome condition gives, for every labeled unit \(i\),
\[
T_1^{-1}\sum_{u=1}^{T_1}\{Y_{iu}(1)-Y_{iu}(0)\}=\beta_i.
\]
Thus \(\beta\) is the causal attributable-effect vector, whereas \(z=m+\beta+\eta\) is the observed-law equation through which it is inferred.

Let \(P\) be the orthogonal projector onto \(L\).  Suppose first that
\[
z=m_0+\beta_0=m_1+\beta_1
\]
are two admissible decompositions and put \(h=\beta_1-\beta_0\).  The support union has size at most \(2s\), and subtraction gives \(h=m_0-m_1\in L\).  Enlarge \(\operatorname{supp}(h)\), if necessary, to a set \(S\subseteq[N]\) of size \(2s\), and write \(h=E_Sx\).  By the definition of \(\kappa_s(L)\),
\[
0=\lVert(I_N-P)h\rVert_2
=\lVert(I_N-P)E_Sx\rVert_2
\ge \kappa_s(L)\lVert x\rVert_2
=\kappa_s(L)\lVert h\rVert_2.
\]
If \(\kappa_s(L)>0\), this forces \(h=0\), hence \(\beta_0=\beta_1\).

Conversely, if \(\kappa_s(L)=0\), finiteness of the collection of sets \(S\) and compactness of their unit spheres give a nonzero \(h\in L\) with \(\lVert h\rVert_2=1\) and \(|\operatorname{supp}(h)|\le2s\).  Partition its support as \(S_0\mathbin{\dot\cup}S_1\), where \(|S_j|\le s\), and write \(h=h_0+h_1\) with \(h_j\) supported on \(S_j\).  Because \(A,B>0\), one may choose
\[
0<c\le \min\{2A,B/\lVert h\rVert_\infty\}.
\]
Define
\[
\beta_0=-ch_1,
\; \beta_1=ch_0,
\; m_0=ch/2,
\; m_1=-ch/2.
\]
Then both effects are \(s\)-sparse and bounded coordinatewise by \(B\), both latent means belong to \(L\) and have norm at most \(A\), and
\[
m_0+\beta_0={c\over2}(h_0-h_1)=m_1+\beta_1,
\; \beta_1-\beta_0=ch\ne0.
\]
To verify the complete-law assertion, retain any admissible pre-panel parameters having loading space \(L\), the same \(D,F,\sigma\), and the same Gaussian error law.  Since \(D\) is invertible by the positive loading-strength assumption, for \(j=0,1\) choose \(a_j=D^{-1}U^{\top}m_j\) and set \(G_j=a_j\mathbf 1_{T_1}^{\top}\).  These post paths have zero centered covariance and zero centered norm, while \(\Lambda a_j=m_j\).  Their observed post means are equal by the preceding display, their post covariance matrices are both \(\sigma^2I\), and their pre laws are identical.  Thus the full laws of \((Y_0,Y_1)\) coincide although \(\beta_0\ne\beta_1\).  This proves both directions.

Put \(X=UDF\), \(\Sigma_0=UD^2U^{\top}+\sigma^2I_N\), and \(\Delta=S_0-\Sigma_0\).  The pre-model and normalization assumptions imply
\[
T_0^{-1}XX^{\top}=UD(T_0^{-1}FF^{\top})DU^{\top}=UD^2U^{\top}.
\]
Writing \(E=E_0\), \(M=XE^{\top}\), and
\[
W=T_0^{-1}(EE^{\top}-T_0\sigma^2I_N),
\]
we therefore have
\[
\Delta=T_0^{-1}(M+M^{\top})+W.
\]
For deterministic \(X\) and independent centered Gaussian entries of \(E\), direct index summation gives
\[
\mathbb E\lVert M\rVert_F^2=N\sigma^2\lVert X\rVert_F^2,
\;
\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}(M^2)=\sigma^2\lVert X\rVert_F^2.
\]
Indeed, in the second identity the covariance \(\mathbb E(E_{jt}E_{iu})=\sigma^2\mathbf 1\{i=j,t=u\}\) leaves exactly \(\sum_{i,t}X_{it}^2\).  Consequently,
\[
\mathbb E\lVert M+M^{\top}\rVert_F^2
=2(N+1)\sigma^2\lVert X\rVert_F^2.
\]
For \(W\), each diagonal entry has variance \(2\sigma^4/T_0\), each off-diagonal entry has variance \(\sigma^4/T_0\), and hence
\[
\mathbb E\lVert W\rVert_F^2={N(N+1)\sigma^4\over T_0}.
\]
The cross term is zero because it is a sum of centered Gaussian third moments.  Finally,
\[
\lVert X\rVert_F^2
=\operatorname{tr}(UDFF^{\top}DU^{\top})
=T_0\operatorname{tr}(D^2).
\]
Combining these equations proves the exact identity
\[
\mathbb E\lVert\Delta\rVert_F^2
={2(N+1)\sigma^2\operatorname{tr}(D^2)+N(N+1)\sigma^4\over T_0}.
\]
The loading and noise bounds imply that its numerator is at most \(V_0\).

It remains to derive, rather than assume, projector control.  The eigenvalues of \(\Sigma_0\) on \(L\) are \(\sigma^2+D_{jj}^2\), while all eigenvalues on \(L^\perp\) equal \(\sigma^2\); the separating gap is therefore at least \(g=d_{\mathrm{lo}}^2\), whether or not the nonzero strengths repeat.  Let \(e=\lVert\widehat P-P\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\).  If \(\lVert\Delta\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\ge g/2\), the elementary bound between equal-rank orthogonal projectors, \(e\le1\), gives \(e\le2\lVert\Delta\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}/g\).  Otherwise, let \(\widehat U\) be an orthonormal eigenbasis for the top \(r\) eigenvalues of \(S_0\), with diagonal eigenvalue matrix \(\widehat H\).  Weyl's variational inequality, obtained directly from the Rayleigh quotient, gives
\[
\lambda_{\min}(\widehat H)\ge\sigma^2+g-\lVert\Delta\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
Projecting \(S_0\widehat U=\widehat U\widehat H\) onto \(L^\perp\), and using \((I_N-P)\Sigma_0=\sigma^2(I_N-P)\), yields
\[
(I_N-P)\widehat U(\widehat H-\sigma^2I_r)=(I_N-P)\Delta\widehat U.
\]
Thus
\[
\lVert(I_N-P)\widehat U\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\le {\lVert\Delta\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\over g-\lVert\Delta\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}}
\le {2\lVert\Delta\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\over g}.
\]
The left side equals \(\lVert\widehat P-P\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\), by the singular-value characterization of principal angles.  Hence, in all cases,
\[
 e\le\min\{1,2\lVert\Delta\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}/d_{\mathrm{lo}}^2\}.
\]
Since \(\lVert\Delta\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le\lVert\Delta\rVert_F\), Cauchy--Schwarz and the exact moment identity give
\[
\mathbb Ee\le\min\{1,2\sqrt{V_0/T_0}/d_{\mathrm{lo}}^2\},
\;
\mathbb Ee^2\le\min\{1,4V_0/(T_0d_{\mathrm{lo}}^4)\}.
\]
If \(\delta_0=1\), every rank-\(r\) orthogonal projector is within operator distance one of \(\widehat P\), so \(P\in\mathcal K_0(Y_0)\) surely.  If \(\delta_0<1\), Markov's inequality applied to \(e^2\) gives
\[
\Pr\{P\notin\mathcal K_0(Y_0)\}
=\Pr(e>\delta_0)
\le{4V_0/(T_0d_{\mathrm{lo}}^4)\over\delta_0^2}
=\alpha/2.
\]
All bounds are uniform because only the displayed class bounds were used.

In the specialization \(N=3,r=s=1\), write \(L=\operatorname{span}(u)\) with \(\lVert u\rVert_2=1\).  For a two-element set \(S\) with complementary index \(i\),
\[
E_S^{\top}(I_3-uu^{\top})E_S=I_2-u_Su_S^{\top},
\]
whose least eigenvalue is \(1-\lVert u_S\rVert_2^2=u_i^2\).  Hence
\[
\kappa_1(L)=\min_{1\le i\le3}|u_i|le {1\over\sqrt3},
\]
with equality if and only if \(|u_1|=|u_2|=|u_3|=1/\sqrt3\).  After quotienting by the irrelevant global sign, these are exactly the four lines indexed by \(h\in\mathcal H_4\), so \(\kappa_\star=1/\sqrt3\).

If \(h\ne h'\) index distinct lines, then \(|u_h^{\top}u_{h'}|=1/3\).  For rank-one projectors the nonzero principal angle gives
\[
\lVert P_h-P_{h'}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
=\sqrt{1-(u_h^{\top}u_{h'})^2}={2\sqrt2\over3}.
\]
Fix the true label \(h\).  If \(\widehat h\ne h\), the nearest-projector rule and the triangle inequality imply
\[
{2\sqrt2\over3}
\le\lVert P_h-P_{\widehat h}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\le\lVert P_h-\widehat P\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
  +\lVert\widehat P-P_{\widehat h}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\le2\lVert\widehat P-P_h\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
Thus misclassification implies \(e^2\ge2/9\).  The squared projector bound already proved is uniform over every profiled \(d,f,\sigma\) in \(\mathcal E_4(T_0)\), and Markov's inequality yields
\[
\sup_{d,f,\sigma}\Pr_{h,d,f,\sigma}(\widehat h\ne h)
\le {9\over2}\,{4V_0\over T_0d_{\mathrm{lo}}^4}
={18V_0\over T_0d_{\mathrm{lo}}^4}.
\]
Taking the minimum with one gives \(p_{\mathrm{cls}}(T_0)\).  If \(T_0\ge\overline T\), the definition of \(\overline T\) gives \(18V_0/(T_0d_{\mathrm{lo}}^4)\le\alpha/2\), completing the proof.

First consider the finite computation and regularity of the output.  For each one of the finitely many sets \(S\subseteq[N]\) with \(|S|\le s\), impose \(b_j=0\) for \(j\notin S\) and introduce variables \((b,P',m')\) satisfying
\[
-B\le b_j\le B,\; P'^{\top}=P',\quad P'^2=P',\quad
\operatorname{tr}(P')=r,\; P'm'=m',\quad
\lVert m'\rVert_2^2\le A^2,
\]
\[
\lVert P'-\widehat P\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta_0,\;
\lVert z-m'-b\rVert_2^2\le\varepsilon_1^2.
\]
The operator-norm inequality is semialgebraic, for example by requiring positive semidefiniteness of \(\delta_0^2I_N-(P'-\widehat P)^2\), expressed through its finitely many principal minors.  Hence this is exactly a finite list of compact semialgebraic feasibility problems, one per support, and its projection onto \(b\) is the defined set \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{\mathrm{ad}}\).  The variable domain is compact and all constraints are closed, so each projected set, and therefore their finite union, is compact.

For completeness, measurability does not require an unproved selection step.  The fixed tie rule makes \(Y_0\mapsto\widehat P\) Borel measurable, and \((Y_0,Y_1)\mapsto(\widehat P,z)\) is therefore Borel.  For a fixed support and a fixed closed subset \(K\) of the coefficient cube, minimize over the fixed compact domain consisting of \(b\in K\) on that support, rank-\(r\) projectors \(P'\), and \(m'\) in the radius-\(A\) ball the maximum of the continuous constraint violations
\[
\lVert P'-\widehat P\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}-\delta_0,\;
\lVert P'm'-m'\rVert_2,\;
\lVert z-m'-b\rVert_2-\varepsilon_1.
\]
Its minimum is a continuous function of \((\widehat P,z)\), by uniform continuity on the fixed compact domain.  Feasibility is the event that this minimum is at most zero.  For an open set \(O\) in the coefficient cube, write \(O\) as the increasing union of the closed sets whose distance from \(O^c\) is at least \(1/n\).  The event that the output hits \(O\) is then a countable union, over \(n\) and the finitely many supports, of the preceding Borel feasibility events.  This proves compact-valued measurability.  The construction nowhere uses \(\gamma\).

Now fix \(\vartheta\in\mathcal M_{T_0,T_1}(0)\).  By the projector-region lemma,
\[
\Pr_\vartheta\{P\in\mathcal K_0(Y_0)\}\ge1-\alpha/2.
\]
By the post-mean law,
\[
{T_1\lVert\eta\rVert_2^2\over\sigma^2}\sim\chi_N^2.
\]
Since \(\sigma\le\sigma_{\mathrm{hi}}\), the definition of \(\varepsilon_1\) gives
\[
\Pr_\vartheta\{\lVert\eta\rVert_2\le\varepsilon_1\}\ge1-\alpha/2.
\]
On the intersection of these two events, take \(P'=P\), \(m'=m\), and \(b=\beta\).  The model assumptions give the support, cube, range, and radius constraints, while \(z-m-\beta=\eta\); hence \(\beta\in\widehat{\mathcal C}_{\mathrm{ad}}\).  The union bound, without any independence requirement, proves coverage at least \(1-\alpha=0.95\), uniformly over the class.  By convention the diameter of an empty or singleton compact set is zero.

For the strict-regime example, take \(N=8,r=2,s=3\), let \(X\) have rows \((1,i)\), \(1\le i\le8\), and set \(U=X(X^{\top}X)^{-1/2}\).  Then \(U^{\top}U=I_2\).  Every two-row submatrix is nonsingular because
\[
\det\begin{pmatrix}1&i\\1&j\end{pmatrix}=j-i\ne0\quad(i\ne j).
\]
There are finitely many such submatrices, so the equivalent deleted-row formula gives \(\kappa_3(\operatorname{col}(U))>0\).  Choosing any sufficiently small vector with exactly three nonzero coordinates supplies a legal positive-margin Gaussian instance covered by the theorem.  HeLiShiMiao2026, Assumption 4 and its identification discussion, impose the majority-valid-controls count whose \(N=8,r=2\) specialization permits at most two affected units; thus this three-effect instance establishes the final comparison.

Write \(a_0=T_0^{-1/2}\), \(a_1=T_1^{-1/2}\), and \(e=\lVert\widehat P-P\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\).  We first prove the upper bound on every sample, including samples on which the true parameter is not accepted.  Take two elements \(b,b'\in\widehat{\mathcal C}_{\mathrm{ad}}\), with witnesses \((P',m',r')\) and \((P'',m'',r'')\), where
\[
z=m'+b+r'=m''+b'+r'',\;
\lVert r'\rVert_2,\lVert r''\rVert_2\le\varepsilon_1.
\]
Set \(h=b-b'\).  It is supported on at most \(2s\) coordinates.  Since \(P'm'=m'\), \(P''m''=m''\), and both accepted projectors are within \(\delta_0\) of \(\widehat P\),
\[
\lVert(I_N-P)m'\rVert_2
\le\lVert P'-P\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\lVert m'\rVert_2
\le A(\delta_0+e),
\]
and the same bound holds for \(m''\).  Projecting
\(h=m''-m'+r''-r'\) onto \(L^\perp\), and using the margin condition, gives, for \(\gamma>0\),
\[
\gamma\lVert h\rVert_2
\le\lVert(I_N-P)h\rVert_2
\le2A(\delta_0+e)+2\varepsilon_1.
\]
Independently, the cube and triangle inequalities give
\[
\lVert h\rVert_2\le2B\sqrt{s},
\;
\lVert h\rVert_2\le\lVert m'-m''\rVert_2+\lVert r'-r''\rVert_2
\le2A+2\varepsilon_1.
\]
Therefore
\[
\operatorname{diam}_2(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{\mathrm{ad}})
\le\min\left\{2B\sqrt{s},\,2A+2\varepsilon_1,
{2\varepsilon_1+2A(\delta_0+e)\over\gamma}\right\},
\]
with the quotient omitted at \(\gamma=0\).  The pre-panel lemma and the definitions imply, for a fixed-class constant \(C_0\),
\[
\varepsilon_1\le C_0a_1,\;
\delta_0+\mathbb Ee\le C_0a_0.
\]
Taking expectations in the pathwise display and using
\[
\min\{A+a_1,x\}\le a_1+\min\{A,x\}
\]
shows
\[
\sup_{\vartheta\in\mathcal M_{T_0,T_1}(\gamma)}
\mathbb E_\vartheta\operatorname{diam}_2(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{\mathrm{ad}})
\le C\min\left\{B\sqrt{s},a_1+\min\left[A,{a_1+Aa_0\over\gamma}\right]\right\}
=C\rho_{\mathrm{ad}}(\gamma).
\]
At \(\gamma=0\), the same conclusion follows from the \(2A+2\varepsilon_1\) bound and the prescribed infinite-quotient convention.  Global honesty was proved above, so the definition of \(R_{\mathrm{ad}}\) gives the first upper inequality.

We next prove a full-observation lower bound.  We use the following elementary two-point fact.  If a confidence set has coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) at laws \(Q_0,Q_1\), with corresponding targets \(b_0,b_1\), then
\[
\mathbb E_{Q_0}\operatorname{diam}_2(\mathcal C)
\ge\lVert b_1-b_0\rVert_2\{1-2\alpha-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\}.
\]
Indeed, under \(Q_0\), the event \(b_0\in\mathcal C\) has probability at least \(1-\alpha\), and the event \(b_1\in\mathcal C\) has probability at least \(1-\alpha-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\); intersect them.  For equal-covariance Gaussian vectors with mean difference \(v\) and covariance \(\sigma^2I\), completing the square gives Hellinger affinity \(\exp\{-\lVert v\rVert_2^2/(8\sigma^2)\}\).  Cauchy--Schwarz applied to the two square-root densities gives
\[
\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)
\le\sqrt{1-\exp\{-\lVert v\rVert_2^2/(4\sigma^2)\}}.
\]
Thus a sufficiently small fixed upper bound on the full Gaussian squared mean distance divided by \(\sigma^2\) makes the brace a positive fixed constant.

We construct three legal pairs.  Nonemptiness of \(\mathcal M_{T_0,T_1}(0)\) supplies one admissible \(D,F,\sigma\); these constraints are independent of the chosen loading frame, and all post factors below are constant.  First keep \(U,D,F,m=0,\sigma\) fixed, take \(\beta_0=0\), and take \(\beta_1=te_j\).  The pre means agree and the squared full post-mean distance is \(T_1t^2\).  With a sufficiently small fixed constant \(c_1>0\),
\[
t=c_1\min\{B,\sigma T_1^{-1/2}\}
\]
gives the lower term \(\min\{B,a_1\}\); both points lie in the same margin stratum.

Second, compactness in the finite support minimum gives, for a loading space with \(\kappa_s(L)=\gamma\), a unit vector \(h\) supported on at most \(2s\) such that
\[
\lVert(I_N-P)h\rVert_2=\gamma,\;
\lVert Ph\rVert_2=\sqrt{1-\gamma^2}.
\]
Such a loading space exists for every \(\gamma\in[0,\kappa_\star]\): the real Grassmannian is connected, \(L\mapsto\kappa_s(L)\) is continuous, a space containing a coordinate vector has margin zero, and a Vandermonde frame has strictly positive margin; compactness then makes its image the full interval from zero to its maximum.  Split the support of \(h\) into two parts of size at most \(s\), so that \(th=\beta_1-\beta_0\) with both effects bounded whenever \(t\le B\).  Put
\[
m_0={t\over2}Ph,\; m_1=-{t\over2}Ph.
\]
The pre laws coincide, while the difference between every post mean column is
\[
(m_1+\beta_1)-(m_0+\beta_0)=t(I_N-P)h
\]
exactly.  Hence the full squared mean distance is \(T_1t^2\gamma^2\).  Taking
\[
t=c_2\min\{B,A,\sigma/(\gamma\sqrt{T_1})\}
\]
for a sufficiently small fixed \(c_2\), with the quotient infinite at zero, gives the lower term
\[
\min\{B,A,a_1/\gamma\}.
\]

Third suppose \(\gamma>0\), use the same minimizing \(h\), and write
\[
h=\rho v+\gamma w,\;
\rho=\sqrt{1-\gamma^2},\quad v\in L,\quad w\in L^\perp,\quad
\lVert v\rVert_2=\lVert w\rVert_2=1.
\]
The dimension condition implies \(\kappa_\star^2\le(N-2s)/N<1\): averaging \(\operatorname{tr}(U_C^{\top}U_C)/r\) over all \((N-2s)\)-subsets \(C\) gives \((N-2s)/N\), and \(\lambda_{\min}\le\operatorname{tr}/r\).  Thus \(\rho>0\).  Let \(M=A/2\), set
\[
m_0=Mv,\; m_1=m_0-th,
\]
and choose \(t\le\min\{B,A/8\}\).  Then \(3A/8\le\lVert m_1\rVert_2\le5A/8\).  Let \(R\) be the rotation in \(\operatorname{span}(v,w)\) that maps \(v\) to \(m_1/\lVert m_1\rVert_2\) and is the identity on the orthogonal complement, and put \(U_1=RU_0\), retaining \(D,F,\sigma\).  Then \(m_1\in\operatorname{col}(U_1)\), and the angle \(\theta\) of this rotation satisfies
\[
\sin\theta={t\gamma\over\lVert m_1\rVert_2}
\le {8t\gamma\over3A}.
\]
Split \(th=\beta_1-\beta_0\) as above.  Since \(m_1=m_0-th\), all post mean columns are exactly equal under the two points.  The pre contribution to the full Gaussian squared mean distance is
\[
\lVert(U_1-U_0)DF\rVert_F^2
=T_0\lVert(U_1-U_0)D\rVert_F^2
\le2T_0d_{\mathrm{hi}}^2\sin^2\theta
\le {128T_0d_{\mathrm{hi}}^2t^2\gamma^2\over9A^2}.
\]
The first point belongs to the \(\gamma\)-stratum; the second is in the global class, which is exactly what global honesty requires.  Taking
\[
t=c_3\min\{B,A,A\sigma/(d_{\mathrm{hi}}\gamma\sqrt{T_0})\}
\]
with a sufficiently small fixed \(c_3\) gives the lower term
\[
\min\{B,A,Aa_0/\gamma\}.
\]
At \(\gamma=0\), the null vector supplied by the sparse-uniqueness proof gives identical full laws and the term \(\min\{B,A\}\).

All these are pairs in the original \((Y_0,Y_1)\) experiment; no noiseless label or oracle loading space has been supplied.  Finally, for nonnegative \(x,y\),
\[
\min\{A,x+y\}\asymp
\max\{\min(A,x),\min(A,y)\},
\]
and \(a_1+q\asymp\max(a_1,q)\), with absolute comparison factors at most two.  Applying these identities with \(x=a_1/\gamma\), \(y=Aa_0/\gamma\), and observing that fixed \(s\) makes \(B\sqrt{s}\asymp B\), the maximum of the three lower terms is comparable to \(\rho_{\mathrm{ad}}(\gamma)\).  The two-point inequality therefore gives \(R_{\mathrm{ad}}(\gamma)\ge c\rho_{\mathrm{ad}}(\gamma)\), uniformly in \(T_0,T_1,\gamma\).  Together with the upper construction, this proves the theorem, including post-noise, compensated-rotation, and bounded-signal saturation channels.

Because \(\mathcal M_{T_0,T_1}(\gamma)\subseteq\mathcal M_{T_0,T_1}(0)\), every globally honest procedure is oracle-honest on the stratum.  Consequently,
\[
R_{\mathrm{or}}(\gamma)\le R_{\mathrm{ad}}(\gamma)\lesssim\rho_{\mathrm{ad}}(\gamma).
\]
At \(\gamma=0\), the two model classes and the two honesty classes coincide, so equality of the two risks and the adaptive-frontier theorem prove the claim.

Fix now \(0<\gamma\le\kappa_\star/2\).  We show that each lower-bound pair used for the adaptive frontier can be kept inside the oracle stratum.  The direct post-noise pair already has a common loading space and lies in that stratum.  The fixed-geometry sparse pair may use a space with margin exactly \(\gamma\), so it also lies entirely in the stratum.  These give
\[
R_{\mathrm{or}}(\gamma)\gtrsim
\max\{\min(B,a_1),\min(B,A,a_1/\gamma)\}.
\]

For the loading-uncertainty term, choose instead a base space \(L_0\) with \(\kappa_s(L_0)=2\gamma\), whose existence follows from the connected attained-range argument in the adaptive-frontier proof.  Apply the same compensated rotation using a unit sparse minimizer for this base margin.  For any two projectors and every support \(S\), singular-value perturbation gives
\[
\left|\sigma_{\min}((I_N-P)E_S)-
\sigma_{\min}((I_N-P')E_S)\right|
\le\lVert(P-P')E_S\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
\le\lVert P-P'\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
Taking the finite minimum over \(S\) proves
\[
|\kappa_s(L)-\kappa_s(L')|\le\lVert P-P'\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.
\]
For the rotation, \(\lVert P_1-P_0\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}=\sin\theta\le16t\gamma/(3A)\).  Multiplying the choice of \(t\) by a sufficiently small fixed constant ensures both \(t\le A/8\) and \(\lVert P_1-P_0\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le\gamma\).  It follows that
\[
\kappa_s(L_1)\ge2\gamma-\gamma=\gamma.
\]
Both points therefore belong to \(\mathcal M_{T_0,T_1}(\gamma)\), their post means agree exactly, and their full pre-panel Gaussian distance is bounded exactly as before.  The oracle two-point inequality yields
\[
R_{\mathrm{or}}(\gamma)\gtrsim\min\{B,A,Aa_0/\gamma\}.
\]
The same elementary max-versus-sum comparison used in the adaptive theorem shows that the maximum of these three terms is comparable to \(\rho_{\mathrm{ad}}(\gamma)\).  This proves
\[
R_{\mathrm{or}}(\gamma)\asymp R_{\mathrm{ad}}(\gamma)
\asymp\rho_{\mathrm{ad}}(\gamma)
\]
uniformly throughout the stated weak-margin range.

The four-line lemma proves \(\kappa_\star=1/\sqrt3\), identifies the endpoint loading lines, and gives
\[
\sup_{\vartheta\in\mathcal M_{T_0,T_1}(1/\sqrt3)}
\Pr_\vartheta(\widehat h\ne h)\le\alpha/2
\;(T_0\ge\overline T).
\]
The post-mean law and the definition of \(\varepsilon_1\) similarly give
\[
\inf_{\vartheta\in\mathcal M_{T_0,T_1}(1/\sqrt3)}
\Pr_\vartheta(\lVert\eta\rVert_2\le\varepsilon_1)\ge1-\alpha/2.
\]
On the intersection, the selected projector is the true endpoint projector and \((b,m')=(\beta,m)\) is feasible for \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{\mathrm{end}}\).  The union bound therefore proves oracle coverage at least \(1-\alpha\).

The diameter bound is pathwise and does not condition on correct classification.  Fix any selected endpoint line with projector \(P_{\widehat h}\), and take two accepted elements \(b,b'\) with witnesses \(m,m'\) and residuals \(r,r'\).  Then
\[
b-b'=m'-m+r'-r,\;
(I_3-P_{\widehat h})(m'-m)=0,\;
\lVert r'-r\rVert_2\le2\varepsilon_1.
\]
Since \(b-b'\) is supported on at most two coordinates and every endpoint line has margin \(1/\sqrt3\),
\[
{1\over\sqrt3}\lVert b-b'\rVert_2
\le\lVert(I_3-P_{\widehat h})(b-b')\rVert_2
\le2\varepsilon_1.
\]
Also, if the supports coincide then \(\lVert b-b'\rVert_2\le2B\), while if they are distinct then \(\lVert b-b'\rVert_2\le\sqrt2B<2B\).  Thus on every realization,
\[
\operatorname{diam}_2(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{\mathrm{end}})
\le\min\{2B,2\sqrt3\varepsilon_1\}.
\]
The procedure is compact-valued and measurable by the same finite-support, fixed-projector argument as for the adaptive set.  Hence
\[
R_{\mathrm{or}}(1/\sqrt3)\lesssim\min\{B,T_1^{-1/2}\}.
\]
For the reverse inequality, keep any endpoint loading line and all nuisance parameters fixed, put \(m=0\), and compare \(\beta_0=0\) with \(\beta_1=te_j\), where \(t=c\min\{B,\sigma T_1^{-1/2}\}\).  Both points remain in the endpoint stratum, their pre laws agree, and their full post Gaussian squared mean distance is \(T_1t^2\).  The two-point calculation from the adaptive theorem gives
\[
R_{\mathrm{or}}(1/\sqrt3)\gtrsim\min\{B,T_1^{-1/2}\}.
\]
The displayed characterization of \(R_{\mathrm{ad}}(1/\sqrt3)\) follows directly from the adaptive-frontier theorem.  Notice that the misclassification event affects only coverage: the diameter inequality used the selected endpoint line and is valid even when that line is wrong, so no classification-error remainder enters expected diameter.

The direct post-noise two-point construction used above shows that \(R_{\mathrm{or}}(\gamma)>0\) for every finite \(T_1\), so the ratio is well defined.  On \(0\le\gamma\le\kappa_\star/2\), the weak-margin theorem gives
\[
c\rho_{\mathrm{ad}}(\gamma)
\le R_{\mathrm{or}}(\gamma),R_{\mathrm{ad}}(\gamma)
\le C\rho_{\mathrm{ad}}(\gamma).
\]
Division proves \(\mathfrak A(\gamma)\asymp1\), uniformly in both sample sizes.

In the specialization \(N=3,r=s=1\), the endpoint proposition and the adaptive-frontier theorem give, for \(T_0\ge\overline T\),
\[
R_{\mathrm{or}}(1/\sqrt3)\asymp\min\{B,T_1^{-1/2}\},
\;
R_{\mathrm{ad}}(1/\sqrt3)\asymp\rho_{\mathrm{ad}}(1/\sqrt3).
\]
The second claimed ratio follows by division.  Along an unsaturated sequence, the outer \(B\)-cap and inner \(A\)-cap in \(\rho_{\mathrm{ad}}\) are eventually inactive.  Since \(B>0\) is fixed and \(T_1\to\infty\), the oracle denominator is then comparable to \(T_1^{-1/2}\), while
\[
\rho_{\mathrm{ad}}(1/\sqrt3)
=T_1^{-1/2}+\sqrt3\{T_1^{-1/2}+AT_0^{-1/2}\}
\asymp T_1^{-1/2}+AT_0^{-1/2}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\mathfrak A(1/\sqrt3)
\asymp {T_1^{-1/2}+AT_0^{-1/2}\over T_1^{-1/2}}
=1+A\sqrt{T_1/T_0}.
\]
This derivation uses only the two regimes for which matching oracle theorems were proved and makes no assertion on the unresolved intermediate-margin region.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Whenever \(\mathcal M_{T_0,T_1}(0)\ne\varnothing\), fix a loading space \(L\) that occurs in that class.  Every decomposition \(z=m+\beta\) with \(m\in L\), \(\lVert m\rVert_2\le A\), \(\lVert\beta\rVert_0\le s\), and \(\lVert\beta\rVert_\infty\le B\) has a unique labeled effect vector \(\beta\) if and only if \(\kappa_s(L)>0\).  If \(\kappa_s(L)=0\), two distinct admissible effect vectors generate the same complete observed-data law with constant post factors.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The complete-observed-law witness is existential and therefore requires a nonempty model class and a loading space realized by that class.  The original statement omitted these boundary conditions; the deterministic uniqueness equivalence itself is unchanged.

proposed.justification: This is the exact identification boundary that makes the margin-indexed inference problem meaningful.
proposed.gap: ChandrasekaranEtAl2011 and FickusMixon2013 contain the generic sparse-subspace geometry; the causal contribution starts after this supporting equivalence.
proposed.consumer: It tells applied users when a full labeled direct-and-spillover vector is distinguishable without selecting valid donors.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A same-sample constant-factor characterization of the oracle expected-diameter frontier on every nonempty margin stratum, including all disconnected-component classification transitions.
open_obligations.obstruction: The explicit sparse-compatible modulus is nonconvex and can jump when its loading-projector radius first reaches a second connected component.  The proved upper and lower bounds evaluate that modulus at different constant multiples of the pre- and post-resolution radii.  No uniform doubling, concavity, or component-testing identity follows from the frozen primitives, so replacing those two radii by one would be an unsupported step, especially near maximal-margin geometries.
open_obligations.attempted: Restricted the support-enumerated confidence inversion to the margin stratum for the upper bound; lifted arbitrary modulus pairs to Procrustes-aligned loading frames with exact normalized pre factors and constant post factors for the original-data Gaussian lower bound; proved the weak-margin rotation regime and the four-line maximal endpoint separately.  A bounded \(N=8,r=2,s=3\) search recovered the harmonic-frame candidate margin \(0.1379496896\) but produced no analytic maximality or component certificate, so it cannot certify a finite component rule.  Extending the rotation argument to intermediate high margins loses stratum membership, while treating separated components by a generic testing error does not yield the exact expected-diameter transition.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Let \(\mathcal G_\gamma=\{L'\in\operatorname{Gr}(r,N):\kappa_s(L')\ge\gamma\}\).  For \(x_0,x_1\ge0\), the strongest proved computable comparison is the compact sparse-compatible modulus
\[
\Omega_\gamma(x_0,x_1)=\sup\lVert b-b'\rVert_2,
\]
where the supremum is over \(L,L'\in\mathcal G_\gamma\), their projectors satisfying \(\lVert P_L-P_{L'}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\le x_0\), vectors \(m\in L\), \(m'\in L'\) with \(\lVert m\rVert_2,\lVert m'\rVert_2\le A\), and \(s\)-sparse \(b,b'\in[-B,B]^N\) satisfying \(\lVert(m+b)-(m'+b')\rVert_2\le x_1\).  Support enumeration makes this a finite union of compact semialgebraic optimizations.  Restricting the global feasibility set to \(\mathcal G_\gamma\) gives the same-sample upper bound
\[
R_{\mathrm{or}}(\gamma)\le
\Omega_\gamma(2\delta_0,2\varepsilon_1).
\]
Conversely, for fixed-class constants \(c,c_0,c_1>0\), Procrustes-aligned loading frames, a common admissible \(D,F,\sigma\), constant post factors, and the two-point confidence-set inequality give
\[
R_{\mathrm{or}}(\gamma)\ge
c\,\Omega_\gamma(c_0T_0^{-1/2},c_1T_1^{-1/2}).
\]
Indeed, a feasible pair at these radii has full pre squared mean distance at most \(2rT_0d_{\mathrm{hi}}^2x_0^2\) and full post squared mean distance at most \(T_1x_1^2\), so its total-variation distance is bounded away from \(1-2\alpha\).  This proves an explicit original-observation modulus sandwich, but not the requested equivalence at one common resolution.
